claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi alloy is a fully disordered, single-phase solid solution.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi for 24–72 hours at 500–600°C induces nanoscale local chemical ordering.
The aging-induced ordered clusters are preferentially localized at or near grain boundaries.
The ordered clusters remain incipient nanodomains rather than evolving into a separate intermetallic phase.
Ordered grain-boundary clusters reduce the alloy's ability to accommodate plastic deformation.
Nanoscale ordered clusters impede dislocation motion.
Reduced atomic randomness and impeded dislocation motion at grain boundaries localize stress.
Stress concentration associated with ordered grain-boundary clusters initiates intergranular cracking and brittle fracture.
The proposed ordering-driven embrittlement mechanism is distinct from conventional precipitation-driven embrittlement.
Aged specimens will have lower ductility than as-quenched or solution-treated controls.
Aged specimens will have lower toughness than as-quenched or solution-treated controls.
Aged specimens will exhibit intergranular cracking or cleavage-like fracture features.
The proposed mechanism is expected to dominate after aging at 500–600°C.
The proposed mechanism is expected to dominate under moderate or high strain-rate loading.
Extreme temperatures or loading rates may activate additional deformation or damage mechanisms.
Subtle nanoprecipitate formation during aging may contribute to any observed brittleness.
The as-quenched or solution-treated baseline has a uniformly disordered microstructure and more ductile behavior.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator specifies ordering without formation of a separate phase, while the uncertainty field allows subtle nanoprecipitate formation to contribute; these are competing descriptions of the aged microstructure.

The main hypothesis says ordering promotes brittle behavior and the uncertainty field explicitly questions whether it acts alone, but the falsification rule reframes the tested hypothesis as one in which local ordering alone governs brittleness.
